$comment: Environment-specific values are not stored in this repository. Prompts keep a
{{TOKEN}} in their place, and the value is supplied when the agent is installed
into a Buzz community.
tokens     — bidirectional. export-agents.mjs swaps the local value out for the
token; restore-agents.mjs swaps a target community's value back in.
redactions — one-way. Text that should never be stored at all, scrubbed on export
and never reinstated. Use for anything personal or dead.
portableOnly — a token that appears only in the artifacts under portable/ and never in a
prompt Buzz receives. No operator holds a value for one, so export-agents.mjs
leaves it out of the "no value for" warning; build-agents.mjs fails if one
ever reaches the Buzz prompt, which is what makes that exemption safe.
deployTokens — the OTHER syntax, @SLUG@ rather than {{TOKEN}}. Expanded once by the deploy
script and never swapped back, where a {{TOKEN}} is swapped bidirectionally on
export. Two lifecycles, which is why there are two syntaxes; do not unify them.
Declaring a client slug as a {{TOKEN}} would make it a substring replaced across
every prompt, which is the footgun described just below.
Most of these are on the canvas of the channel the install is being run in, which is
where to look before asking anybody for one. nest/.claude/skills/deploy-agents/SKILL.md
holds the canvas-key-to-token map and the canonical canvas layout.
Only declared tokens belong in local-values.json. Every value in that file is treated
as a substring to replace on export, so adding a short one — a client slug, a person's
first name — rewrites unrelated words in prompts that happen to contain it.

BQ_PROJECT.description: Google Cloud project holding the BigQuery datasets Claire reads.
BQ_PROJECT.howToFind: Canvas key `bq_project` in the install channel. Otherwise: Google Cloud console → project picker → the project ID (not the display name).

BUILDER_REPO.description: owner/name of the prototype repository ALAN builds in.
BUILDER_REPO.howToFind: Canvas key `builder_repo` in the install channel. Otherwise: the GitHub path of the repo ALAN should build prototypes in.

BUILDER_REPO_NAME.description: Bare repository name from BUILDER_REPO. Used for checkout paths.
BUILDER_REPO_NAME.howToFind: The part of BUILDER_REPO after the slash. Derived from canvas key `builder_repo`, not looked up.

KNOWLEDGE_REPO_NAME.description: Bare name of the design-knowledge repository ALAN promotes findings into and must never edit directly.
KNOWLEDGE_REPO_NAME.howToFind: Canvas key `knowledge_repo` in the install channel. The repository holding the design-rule skills, which ALAN promotes findings into and must never edit directly.

TRANSCRIPT_DIR.description: Directory holding the agent session transcripts Janice reads as evidence. Contains one <session-id>.jsonl per session.
TRANSCRIPT_DIR.howToFind: Claude Code writes transcripts to ~/.claude/projects/<encoded-cwd>/, where the encoded name is the agent nest's absolute path with each slash and dot replaced by a dash — /Users/you/.buzz becomes -Users-you--buzz. bootstrap-nest.mjs derives this for you.

TAG_SHEET_ID.description: Google Sheet holding the shared tag dictionary every research channel tags against. Research taxonomy, no client content.
TAG_SHEET_ID.howToFind: Canvas key `tag_sheet` in the install channel. Otherwise: open the Tag Dictionary sheet; it is the part of the URL between /d/ and /edit. Must be shared as Viewer with the claire-tag-dictionary-reader service account — see Step 0 of CLAIRE_ZERO_TO_RUNNING.md.

DRIVE_FOLDER.description: Drive folder id for one client. The entire world a channel's Drive service account can see.
DRIVE_FOLDER.howToFind: Canvas key `drive_folder` in the install channel. Otherwise: open the client folder in Drive; it is the part of the URL after /folders/.

CLAIRE_CHANNEL.description: UUID of the building-claire channel in this community. Janice routes findings about Claire here.
CLAIRE_CHANNEL.howToFind: Canvas key `claire_channel` in the install channel. Otherwise `buzz channels list`, or the channel header in Buzz. This is Janice's routing table, not the channel the install runs in.

STU_CHANNEL.description: UUID of the building-stu channel in this community. Janice routes findings about Stu here.
STU_CHANNEL.howToFind: Canvas key `stu_channel` in the install channel. Otherwise `buzz channels list`, or the channel header in Buzz. This is Janice's routing table, not the channel the install runs in.

ALAN_CHANNEL.description: UUID of the building-alan channel in this community. Janice routes findings about ALAN here.
ALAN_CHANNEL.howToFind: Canvas key `alan_channel` in the install channel. Otherwise `buzz channels list`, or the channel header in Buzz. This is Janice's routing table, not the channel the install runs in.

JANICE_CHANNEL.description: UUID of the building-janice channel in this community. Janice's wake messages land here, and it is the fallback for findings about an agent with no channel of its own.
JANICE_CHANNEL.howToFind: Canvas key `janice_channel` in the install channel. Otherwise `buzz channels list`, or the channel header in Buzz. This is Janice's routing table, not the channel the install runs in.

JANICE_PUBKEY.description: Hex pubkey of the Janice instance on this machine, used by the wake hook to address her. One per operator, not one per community.
JANICE_PUBKEY.howToFind: Not on the canvas: each operator runs their own Janice, so this is per-machine, not per-community, and it does not exist until that Janice's draft has been saved. Then: buzz channels members --channel <janice-channel-uuid>, or the agent's profile in Buzz Desktop. Bootstrap therefore runs twice; it is idempotent.

WORKSPACE_ROOT.description: Directory holding the repository checkouts an agent works in. Appears only in the portable artifacts under portable/ — never in a prompt Buzz receives, which is what portableOnly means. On a Buzz install the equivalent path is written out in full; on a plain checkout it is wherever the operator keeps their repos.
WORKSPACE_ROOT.howToFind: Nothing to find on a Buzz machine — leave it unset. Whoever ports the agent fills it in with their own checkout directory.

$redactionsComment: Two kinds of rule live here, and the difference decides whether the guard works on
somebody else's machine.
The one-way replacements above are content-specific: a known bad sentence, and the
text that should stand in its place.
The rules marked `structural: true` match a SHAPE rather than a value. They exist
because the rules that catch client names by name live in local-redactions.json,
which is gitignored and rebuilt per machine from whichever datasets that operator
can read. A slug present in one operator's file is absent from another's — which is
exactly how a client dataset name reached a commit message in a public repo while
the checker returned clean. A shape rule needs no local file and no foreknowledge of
the client, so it holds on a fresh clone.
Client identifiers in this stack are conventional, which is what makes this possible:
a dataset is research_<slug>, an account is claire-<slug>-service-user. The negative
lookaheads exempt the documented placeholders — acme, building_claire, <slug>,
{{TOKEN}} and @dataset — so the guides and templates that must show the shape still
pass. Add a new example slug to the lookahead rather than deleting the rule.
A rule with `$disabled` is skipped by check-text-for-names.mjs, so a rule that turns
out to be too broad can be parked with the reason instead of deleted and re-derived.
One caveat learned the hard way while writing this file: a lookahead is part of the
pattern and the pattern is committed, so exempting a real client by name puts that
name in the tree. Exempt the placeholder, never the client. The structural rules
below caught exactly that mistake in this file on the first sweep.
An MCP-server rule for bq-<slug> and drive-<slug> was tried and withdrawn: bq-channel,
bq-exec and drive-fence are all legitimate, and the exemption list it needed was where
the mistake above happened.

redactions.pattern: and several links point at `/Users/[^`]+`, which does not exist\.
redactions.replace: and several links point at absolute paths on a previous maintainer's machine, which no longer resolve.
redactions.reason: Named a person and their local filesystem layout. The instruction only needs the fact that the links are dead.

SLUG.description: Short lowercase name for one client. Expanded into subagent names, MCP server names and prose.

DATASET.description: Fully-qualified BigQuery dataset for that client, as project.dataset.
